page: Vultr voc-s-8c-64gb-1280s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The underlying hardware features an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor operating at 2.0 GHz, structured with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core. Local storage is bundled with a 1280 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU architecture supports instruction sets such as AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and FMA, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance and PassMark CPU scores align with the middle 50% average, reflecting the 8-vCPU constraint under heavy parallel loads. Memory subsystem performance is robust, with PassMark memory scores ranking in the top 25%, while large-block read and write memory bandwidths average 127.29 GB/sec and 75.3 GB/sec respectively. For specialized workloads, the server exhibits average performance in Redis SET operations at 15.7 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 8.62 GB/sec, but shows a performance bottleneck in medium-model LLM prompt processing, which registers in the bottom 25% at 23.58 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a high density of memory and local NVMe storage relative to its compute core count, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores, a 1:8 memory ratio, and fast NVMe storage makes this instance well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, and moderate data-processing pipelines. However, the lack of GPU acceleration and lower multi-threaded LLM inference speeds make it less suitable for heavy machine learning training or large-scale AI inference.
description: The Vultr voc-s-8c-64gb-1280s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 8 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of RAM and a 1280 GB NVMe SSD. It delivers strong single-core CPU and memory performance, ranking in the top 25% in benchmarks, while multi-core compute and memory bandwidth remain average. With a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and fast local NVMe storage, this server provides a balanced, cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. It is highly suitable for hosting databases, caching layers, and general-purpose web applications, though its lack of GPU acceleration and average multi-core scaling limit its utility for heavy parallel computing or large-scale AI inference.
